author: reek
body: An Aura (Enchant creature) resolves attached to the creature it targeted: its permanent records attached-to = that creature's id, and the enchanted creature's effective power/toughness (in GameState) reads the boost off every Aura attached to it. A non-Aura permanent (creature, global enchantment, artifact) attaches to nothing (attached-to stays -1).

author: reek
body: A keyword-granting Aura (Flight, Lance, Web) bakes its GainKeyword keywords into the enchanted creature at attach time, so every combat keyword check (Flying evasion, first strike, reach) sees them. In this engine Auras are not removed mid-game, so the grant is applied once on resolution rather than summed at read time (unlike the power/toughness boost, which stays dynamic via aura-power).

author: reek
body: One-shot effects that fire as an Aura attaches. Paralyze taps the creature it enchants when it enters (the enchanted creature then also fails to untap -- see Turn.untap-restricted). Other at-attach auras hook in here.

author: reek
body: Triggered abilities fire when their condition occurs: enters-the-battlefield as a permanent resolves, dies as a creature is destroyed. fire-triggers walks a permanent's abilities and applies every TriggeredAbility whose condition matches the one that just happened. Effects are applied immediately with a target chosen in the engine: controller-directed effects (draw, gain life) need none; targeted effects (damage, destroy, exile, bounce) hit the opponent's biggest creature; life loss hits the opponent. A permanent with no matching trigger is left unchanged.

author: reek
body: Nevinyrral's Disk: destroy every artifact, creature, and enchantment (lands survive). Same shape as the Wrath sweep -- each non-land permanent goes through destroy-permanent so its dies triggers fire, and the index resets as the battlefield shrinks.

author: reek
body: Tranquility: destroy every enchantment (global enchantments and auras), leaving creatures, artifacts, and lands. Same shrink-safe shape as the nonland sweep -- each enchantment goes through destroy-permanent so any leave triggers fire, and the index holds while the battlefield shrinks under it.

author: reek
body: Reanimation (Reanimate, Animate Dead): put a target creature card from a graveyard onto the battlefield under the caster's control. Each target is a card id; reanimate-one finds whichever graveyard holds it, removes one copy, and puts a fresh permanent (summoning-sick, controlled by the caster) onto the battlefield. A card in no graveyard is a harmless no-op.

author: reek
body: Regrowth: return target card from the caster's graveyard to hand. Each target is a card id in the controller's graveyard; return-card-from-graveyard removes one copy and adds it to hand, and only when the card was actually there (the graveyard shrank), so a missing target is a harmless no-op.

author: reek
body: Wrath of God: destroy every creature on the battlefield, both players'. Each goes through destroy-permanent so its dies triggers fire and it reaches its owner's graveyard. The index resets whenever the battlefield shrinks, so the walk stays valid as creatures leave.

author: reek
body: Discard sends cards from the target player's hand to the graveyard, from the back of the hand. Mind Rot and Hymn to Tourach were engine no-ops.

author: reek
body: Exile removes a permanent to its owner's exile zone (Swords to Plowshares, Exile effects); bounce returns it to its owner's hand as its card (Unsummon, Boomerang). Both were engine no-ops, so those spells did nothing.
